pieces.title: literals
pieces.source:
use IO.Std.write_line

entry() is
    assert "string literal".get_type() == typeof string
    write_line("string literal")

    assert "string literal with interpolated expressions: {123 + 456} and {789}".get_type() == typeof string
    write_line("string literal with interpolated expressions: {123 + 456} and {789}")

    assert 'c'.get_type() == typeof char
    write_line("char literal: {'c'}")

    assert 123 .get_type() == typeof int
    write_line("integer literal: {123}")

    assert 123_456.789e6D .get_type() == typeof double
    write_line("double literal: {123_456.789e6D}")

    assert ("three", "string", "tuple").get_type() == typeof (string,string,string)
    write_line("tuple literal: {("three", "string", "tuple")}")

    assert ["a", "four", "element", "list"].get_type() == typeof string[]
    write_line("list literal: {["a", "four", "element", "list"] |> $}")
si

pieces.title: control flow
pieces.source:
use IO.Std.write_line
use Ghul.Pipes.index
use Ghul.Pipes.cursor
use Ghul.Pipes.first

entry() is
    assert_examples()
    if_examples()
    if_expression_examples()
    while_examples()
    while_let_examples()
    for_examples()
    try_examples()
    let_use_examples()
si

assert_examples() is
    // assert tests a condition, and throws an exception if the condition does not hold:
    assert 1 == 1
    assert 3 > 2

    // the optional assert else clause supplies a message to include in any thrown exception:
    assert true else "who knows what to believe?"

    // or a specific object to throw:
    assert 1 < "hello".length else System.IndexOutOfRangeException()
si


if_examples() is
    if true then
        assert true
        write_line("true is {true}")
    fi

    if false \/ true then
        write_line("false or-else true is {false \/ true}")
    else
        assert false
    fi
si

if_expression_examples() is
    // if is an expression: its value is the value of the branch that runs.
    // case works the same way when there are more choices - see the
    // pattern-matching example:

    let day_of_week = System.DateTime(2026, 9, 28).day_of_week

    let greeting =
        if day_of_week == System.DayOfWeek.MONDAY then
            "ugh: monday"
        elif day_of_week == System.DayOfWeek.FRIDAY then
            "woooo: friday!"
        else
            "meh: {day_of_week.to_string().to_lower()}"
        fi

    write_line(greeting)
si

while_examples() is
    let i mut = 0

    while i < 10 do
        assert i < 10
        i = i + 1

        write_line("loop iteration {i} out of 10")
    od

    assert i == 10
si

while_let_examples() is
    // while let re-tests its pattern each iteration and declares the
    // present value as a local; the loop ends the first time it is absent
    let remaining mut = 3

    while let n = countdown(remaining) do
        write_line("{n}...")
        remaining = remaining - 1
    od

    write_line("liftoff!")
si

// return the next count while positive, or nothing once it reaches zero
countdown(n: int) -> int? is
    if n > 0 then return n; fi

    return null
si

for_examples() is
    let count mut = 0

    for i in 0..10 do
        assert i >= 0 /\ i < 10

        write_line("i is {i}, count is {count}")

        count = count + 1
    od

    assert count == 10

    // 0..10 is not for loop specific syntax, '..' is just an operator that constructs
    // an iterable integer range:

    let range = 0..100

    assert range.from == 0
    assert range.to == 100

    assert range |> Ghul.Pipes.count() == 100

    // for can iterate over anything that implements Iterable[T], Iterator[T], or move_next() and current:
    for ci in "hello" |> index() do
        write_line("char {ci.index} of 'hello' is {ci.value}")
    od
si

try_examples() is
    try
        let wombat = "wombat"
        let elephant = "elephant"

        write_line("we're pretty sure a {wombat} is the same as an {elephant}, right?")

        assert wombat =~ elephant
    catch ex: System.Exception
        assert ex.get_type() == typeof Ghul.AssertFailedException

        write_line("err, maybe not: {ex.message}")
    yrt

    // try finally for ensuring clean-up code is run:

    let is_resource_in_use mut = false

    try
        is_resource_in_use = true
        write_line("resource acquired")
        throw System.Exception("oops: exception with resource held")
    catch ex: System.Exception
        write_line("caught: {ex.message}")
    finally
        is_resource_in_use = false
        write_line("resource released")
    yrt

    assert !is_resource_in_use

    write_line("done")
si

let_use_examples() is
    let use reader = IO.File.open_text("greeting.txt")

    write_line(reader.read_line())

    // reader will be disposed at the end of the block
    // it was declared in

    // use also works on an expression: it gives back its value, and disposes
    // of it at the end of the block. here it holds the file's lines, so first
    // can stop reading early without leaving the file open:
    let first_line =
        cursor(use IO.File.read_lines("greeting.txt").iterator) |> first()

    write_line(first_line ?? "(empty)")
si

pieces.title: expression-oriented code
pieces.source:
use IO.Std.write_line

entry() is
    expression_bodies()
    if_expressions()
    case_expressions()
    let_in_expressions()
    block_expressions()
    loop_as_expression()
    return_from_block()
    block_as_function_body()
    assert_in_expressions()
si

// an expression-bodied function uses '=>' and a single value - no
// statements, no explicit return:
double(n: int) -> int => n * 2
abs(n: int) -> int => if n < 0 then -n else n fi

expression_bodies() is
    write_line("double(21): {double(21)}")
    write_line("abs(-7): {abs(-7)}")
si

// an if can be used as an expression: its value is the value of the
// branch that runs:
if_expressions() is
    let n = 7

    let parity = if n % 2 == 0 then "even" else "odd" fi
    write_line("{n} is {parity}")

    let sign =
        if n > 0 then "positive"
        elif n < 0 then "negative"
        else "zero"
        fi
    write_line("sign: {sign}")
si

// a case can be used as an expression too; here it needs an else arm,
// and one arm can match several values:
grade(score: int) -> string =>
    case score / 10
    when 10, 9 then "A"
    when 8 then "B"
    when 7 then "C"
    when 6 then "D"
    else "F"
    esac

case_expressions() is
    write_line("95: {grade(95)}")
    write_line("82: {grade(82)}")
    write_line("71: {grade(71)}")
    write_line("40: {grade(40)}")
si

// let ... in names some values for use in a single following
// expression, without opening a block:
let_in_expressions() is
    let area =
        let width = 4, height = 3 in
        width * height
    write_line("area: {area}")

    let size =
        let x = 10 in
        if x > 5 then "big" else "small" fi
    write_line("size: {size}")
si

// a parenthesised block is an expression: a sequence of statements whose
// value is the value of the last one. it can be used anywhere a value
// is needed:
block_expressions() is
    let hypotenuse_squared =
        (
            let a = 3
            let b = 4
            a * a + b * b
        )
    write_line("3,4 -> {hypotenuse_squared}")
si

// a block can run a loop that updates a mut variable, then end
// with that variable as its value:
loop_as_expression() is
    let sum =
        (
            let acc mut = 0
            for i in 1..11 do
                acc = acc + i
            od
            acc
        )
    write_line("sum 1..10: {sum}")

    let factorial =
        (
            let product mut = 1
            for i in 1..6 do
                product = product * i
            od
            product
        )
    write_line("5!: {factorial}")
si

// a return inside a block that is not the whole function body
// exits the block, not the function: it sets the block's value, and
// the code after the block still runs:
return_from_block() is
    let first_positive =
        (
            for x in [-3, -1, 4, 9] do
                if x > 0 then
                    return "{x}"
                fi
            od
            "none"
        )
    write_line("first positive: {first_positive}")
si

// when a block is the whole '=>' body it works like a normal
// block body: return exits the function, and the trailing expression
// supplies the value for any path that does not return early:
sign_label(n: int) -> string =>
    (
        if n < 0 then
            return "neg"
        fi
        if n == 0 then
            return "zero"
        fi
        "pos"
    )

block_as_function_body() is
    write_line("sign_label(-5): {sign_label(-5)}")
    write_line("sign_label(0): {sign_label(0)}")
    write_line("sign_label(5): {sign_label(5)}")
si

// assert ... in checks a condition as part of an expression: if the
// assert fails it throws, otherwise the following expression is the
// result:
checked_head(xs: int[]) -> int =>
    assert xs.count > 0 else "empty" in
    xs[0]

assert_in_expressions() is
    write_line("head of [10,20,30]: {checked_head([10, 20, 30])}")
si

pieces.title: unions
pieces.source:
use IO.Std.write_line

union Option[T] is
    NONE
    SOME(value: T)
si

union List[T] is
    NIL
    CONS(head: T, tail: List[T])
si

union Tree[T] is
    LEAF(value: T)
    NODE(left: Tree[T], right: Tree[T])
si

use Option.SOME
use Option.NONE
use List.NIL
use List.CONS
use Tree.LEAF
use Tree.NODE

list_example[T](elements: Collections.List[T]) -> string =>
    assert elements.count == 3 else "expected 3 elements" in

    let
        list = CONS(elements[0], CONS(elements[1], CONS(elements[2], NIL))),
        stringify_list = l rec =>
            if let (head, tail): CONS = l then
                "{head}, {rec(tail)}"
            else
                "nil"
            fi
    in
        stringify_list(list)

tree_example[T](leaves: Collections.List[T]) -> string =>
    assert leaves.count == 4 else "expected 4 leaves" in

    let tree =
        NODE(
            NODE(
                LEAF(leaves[0]),
                LEAF(leaves[1])
            ),
            NODE(
                LEAF(leaves[2]),
                LEAF(leaves[3])
            )
        )
    in

    let stringify_tree = t rec =>
        if let (left, right): NODE = t then
            // if it's a NODE, recursively stringify the
            // left and right subtrees
            "({rec(left)}, {rec(right)})"
        else
            // if it's not a NODE, it must be a LEAF, so
            // stringify the value
            "{t.value}"
        fi
    in

    stringify_tree(tree)

let some_int = SOME(42)
let none_int = NONE

// isa SOME(o) tests the variant and narrows o to it, so o.value is reachable
let stringify_option = o rec =>
    if isa SOME(o) then
        "{o.value}"
    else
        "none"
    fi

write_line(stringify_option(some_int))
write_line(stringify_option(none_int))

write_line(list_example([1, 2, 3]))
write_line(list_example(["A", "B", "C"]))
write_line(tree_example([1, 2, 3, 4]))
write_line(tree_example(["A", "B", "C", "D"]))

streams
pieces.source:
use IO.Std.write_line
use Ghul.Pipes.STREAM
use Ghul.Pipes.stream
use Ghul.Pipes.filter
use Ghul.Pipes.take
use Ghul.Pipes.zip
use Ghul.Pipes.index

use STREAM.DONE

// stream(initial, advance) builds a lazy sequence, a T{}, from a start state and
// a step function S -> STREAM[T, S]. the step returns DONE to stop, or
// value || next_state to yield the next value.

// count down from n to 1:
let counting = n =>
    stream(n, i => if i == 0 then DONE else i || (i - 1) fi)

// infinite fibonacci, with the last two numbers as the state:
let fibonacci = stream(
    (prev = 1, current = 1),
    (prev, current) => current || (prev = current, current = prev + current)
)

// factorial, with the count and the last value as the state:
let factorial = stream(
    (n = 1, prev = 1),
    (n, prev) => let next_n = n + 1, next = prev * next_n in
        next || (n = next_n, prev = next)
)

// the characters of a string, with an index as the state:
let chars_of = s =>
    let xs = s.to_char_array() in
    stream(0, i => if i == xs.count then DONE else xs[i] || (i + 1) fi)

write_line("counting down from 5: {counting(5)}")
write_line("chars of hello: {chars_of("hello")}")

write_line("first 10 fibonacci numbers: {fibonacci |> take(10)}")
write_line("first 10 factorial numbers: {factorial |> take(10)}")
write_line("first 10 even fibonacci numbers: {fibonacci |> filter(x => x % 2 == 0) |> take(10)}")

for (i, (fib, fact)) in fibonacci |> zip(factorial) |> take(10) |> index() do
    write_line("fibonacci {i} is {fib}")
    write_line("factorial {i} is {fact}")
od

pieces.title: comprehensions
object-oriented programming
pieces.source:
use IO.Std.write_line
use Ghul.Pipes.map

entry() is
    let int_calculator = CALCULATOR(
        [
            ("+", INTEGER_ADDITION()),
            ("-", INTEGER_SUBTRACTION()),
            ("*", INTEGER_MULTIPLICATION()),
            ("/", INTEGER_DIVISION())
        ]
    )

    write_line("1 + 2 = {int_calculator.calculate("+", 1, 2)}")
    write_line("1 - 2 = {int_calculator.calculate("-", 1, 2)}")
    write_line("1 * 2 = {int_calculator.calculate("*", 1, 2)}")
    write_line("1 / 2 = {int_calculator.calculate("/", 1, 2)}")

    write_line("1 + 2 - 3 = {int_calculator.calculate_from_memory("-", 3)}")

    let string_calculator = CALCULATOR(
        [
            ("+", STRING_CONCATENATION()),
            ("-", STRING_SUBTRACTION())
        ]
    )

    write_line("hello + world = {string_calculator.calculate("+", "hello", "world")}")
    write_line("helloworld - world = {string_calculator.calculate("-", "helloworld", "world")}")

    string_calculator.clear_memory()

    write_line("memory is cleared")
si

trait Operation[T] is
    execute(left: T, right: T) -> T
si

class CALCULATOR[V] is
    _operations: Collections.MAP[string, Operation[V]]

    memory: V

    init(operations: Collections.Iterable[(name: string, operation: Operation[V])]) is
        _operations =
            Collections.MAP(
                operations |>
                    map(on => let (name, operation) = on in Collections.KeyValuePair(name, operation)))
    si

    calculate(operation_name: string, left: V, right: V) -> V =>
        if _operations.contains_key(operation_name) then
            let operation = _operations[operation_name]
            memory = operation.execute(left, right)

            memory
        else
            throw System.InvalidOperationException("invalid operation {operation_name}")
        fi


    calculate_from_memory(operation_name: string, right: V) -> V =>
        if _operations.contains_key(operation_name) then
            let operation = _operations[operation_name]
            memory = operation.execute(memory, right)

            memory
        else
            throw System.InvalidOperationException("invalid operation {operation_name}")
        fi

    clear_memory() is
        memory = _
    si
si

class INTEGER_ADDITION(): Operation[int] is
    execute(left: int, right: int) -> int => left + right
si

class INTEGER_SUBTRACTION(): Operation[int] is
    execute(left: int, right: int) -> int => left - right
si

class INTEGER_MULTIPLICATION(): Operation[int] is
    execute(left: int, right: int) -> int => left * right
si

class INTEGER_DIVISION(): Operation[int] is
    execute(left: int, right: int) -> int =>
        if right == 0 then
            throw System.InvalidOperationException("division by zero")
        else
            left / right
        fi
si

class STRING_CONCATENATION(): Operation[string] is
    execute(left: string, right: string) -> string => "{left}{right}"
si

class STRING_SUBTRACTION(): Operation[string] is
    execute(left: string, right: string) -> string => left.replace(right, "")
si

pieces.title: unions
pieces.source:
use IO.Std.write_line

entry() is
    shape_areas()
    labelling_shapes()
    describing_shapes()
    lookups()
si

// a union holds one of a fixed set of variants. the fields in its header are
// shared by every variant, which takes them with '..'. a variant with no
// fields of its own can leave out the parentheses and the '..'.
union Shape(name: string) is
    RECTANGLE(.., width: int, height: int)
    SQUARE(.., side: int)
    POINT
si

use Shape.RECTANGLE
use Shape.SQUARE
use Shape.POINT

// methods are added to a union in a partial block. this case covers every
// variant, so it doesn't need an else arm.
partial Shape is
    area() -> int =>
        case self
        when r: RECTANGLE then r.width * r.height
        when s: SQUARE then s.side * s.side
        when _: POINT then 0
        esac
si

shape_areas() is
    let shapes = [
        RECTANGLE("billboard", 6, 3),
        SQUARE("tile", 4),
        POINT("pixel")
    ]

    for shape in shapes do
        // name is a shared field, readable on any variant
        write_line("{shape.name} has area {shape.area()}")
    od
si

labelling_shapes() is
    write_line(label(SQUARE("badge", 2)))
    write_line(label(POINT("dot")))
si

label(shape: Shape) -> string =>
    // isa V(x) tests the runtime variant and narrows x to it in the
    // branch, so the variant's own fields become readable
    if isa SQUARE(shape) then
        "{shape.name} is a {shape.side}x{shape.side} square"
    elif isa RECTANGLE(shape) then
        "{shape.name} is a {shape.width}x{shape.height} rectangle"
    else
        "{shape.name} is a point"
    fi

// an impl block makes the union implement a trait without naming the trait
// in the union's header. inside it, self is a Shape.
trait Describable is
    describe() -> string
si

impl Describable for Shape is
    describe() -> string =>
        "{name}: area {area()}"
si

describing_shapes() is
    // Shape implements Describable, so a Shape can be passed where a
    // Describable is expected
    let items = Collections.LIST[Describable]()

    items.add(SQUARE("stamp", 2))
    items.add(RECTANGLE("card", 5, 2))

    for item in items do
        write_line(item.describe())
    od
si

// a union with a single field-carrying variant is option shaped: '?'
// tests for that variant and '!' unwraps its field.
union Lookup is
    FOUND(port: int)
    MISSING
si

use Lookup.FOUND
use Lookup.MISSING

lookups() is
    write_line(port_message("http", find_port("http")))
    write_line(port_message("smtp", find_port("smtp")))
si

find_port(scheme: string) -> Lookup is
    if scheme == "http" then return FOUND(80); fi

    return MISSING
si

port_message(scheme: string, result: Lookup) -> string =>
    if result? then
        "{scheme} is on port {result!}"
    else
        "{scheme} has no known port"
    fi

badge is a 2x2 square
dot is a point

pieces.title: pattern matching
pieces.source:
use IO.Std.write_line
use Ghul.Pipes.find

entry() is
    optional_matching()
    type_matching()
    destructuring()
    literal_patterns()
    chained_clauses()
    case_expressions()
    case_binding_patterns()
    if_let_guards()
    case_arm_guards()
    match_by_value()
    while_let_examples()
    nested_destructuring()
si

optional_matching() is
    write_line(greet(find_cat("Felix")))
    write_line(greet(find_cat("Nobody")))
si

greet(maybe_a_cat: CAT?) -> string =>
    // maybe_a_cat is an optional CAT
    // its value can be a CAT, or nothing

    // if let with no pattern matches if a value is present
    if let definitely_a_cat = maybe_a_cat then
        // definitely_a_cat is a CAT
        definitely_a_cat.meow()
    else
        "no such cat"
    fi


find_cat(name: string) -> CAT? =>
    let
        cats = [CAT("Felix"), CAT("Eric"), CAT("Geoff")]
    in
        cats |> find(c => c.name == name)


type_matching() is
    write_line(describe(CAT("Felix")))
    write_line(describe(DOG("Rex")))
    write_line(describe(ANIMAL("Gerald")))
si

describe(a: ANIMAL) -> string =>
    // if let with a type matches if the value is of a compatible type
    if let cat: CAT = a then
        cat.meow()
    elif let dog: DOG = a then
        dog.bark()
    else
        "{a.name} is some other animal"
    fi

destructuring() is
    write_line(show(SCORE("Alice", 10)))
    write_line(show(null))
    write_line(show(pick_winner(SCORE("Bob", 99), SCORE("Alice", 10))))
    write_line(show(pick_winner(SCORE("Alice", 99), SCORE("Bob", 99))))
si

show(score: SCORE?) -> string =>
    if let (who, points) = score then
        "{who} scored {points}"
    else
        "no score"
    fi

// pick the higher scorer, or null for a draw
pick_winner(a: SCORE, b: SCORE) -> SCORE? =>
    let
        (_, a_points) = a,
        (_, b_points) = b
    in
        if a_points > b_points then
            a
        elif b_points > a_points then
            b
        else
            null
        fi

literal_patterns() is
    write_line(label(("nothing", 0)))
    write_line(label(("life the universe and everything", 42)))
    write_line(label(("lucky", 7)))
    write_line(label(null))
si

label(pair: (name: string, value: int)?) -> string =>
    // if let with a destructuring pattern matches if
    // the value is present and the corresponding elements
    // of the value match
    if let (name, 0) = pair then
        "{name} is zero"
    elif let (name, 42) = pair then
        "{name} is the answer"
    elif let (name, n) = pair then
        "{name} is {n}"
    else
        "nothing"
    fi

chained_clauses() is
    let full = ORDER(1, CUSTOMER("Ada", CONTACT("ada@example.com")))
    let no_contact = ORDER(2, CUSTOMER("Bjarne", null))
    let guest = ORDER(3, null)

    write_line(reach(full))
    write_line(reach(no_contact))
    write_line(reach(guest))

    write_line(who(full))
    write_line(who(guest))
si

reach(order: ORDER) -> string =>
    // a single if let can chain comma-separated clauses; every clause
    // must be present for the then-arm to run, and a later clause can
    // use the locals declared by an earlier one
    if let customer = order.customer, contact = customer.contact then
        "order {order.id}: reach {customer.name} at {contact.email}"
    else
        "order {order.id}: no contact on file"
    fi

who(order: ORDER) -> string =>
    // the path shorthand declares a local named after the path's last
    // member, and matches when the whole path is present
    if let order.customer then
        customer.name
    else
        "guest"
    fi

case_expressions() is
    write_line("describe(-1): {describe_int(-1)}")
    write_line("describe(2): {describe_int(2)}")
    write_line("describe(7): {describe_int(7)}")
    write_line("describe(42): {describe_int(42)}")

    write_line(classify((0, 0)))
    write_line(classify((0, 5)))
    write_line(classify((3, 0)))
    write_line(classify((3, 4)))
si

describe_int(n: int) -> string =>
    // case expression matches on the value of n
    case n
    when -1 then
        "minus one"
    when 0 then
        "zero"
    when 1, 2, 3 then
        "small"
    when 4, 5, 6 then
        "medium"
    when 7, 8, 9 then
        "large"
    when 13 then
        "unlucky"
    else
        "other"
    esac

classify(p: (int, int)) -> string =>
    // case expressions support the same patterns as if let
    // so we can destructure the value and match on the elements
    case p
    when (0, 0) then
        "origin"
    when (0, y) then
        "on y axis at {y}"
    when (x, 0) then
        "on x axis at {x}"
    when (x, y) then
        "({x}, {y})"
    esac

class ANIMAL(name: string)

class CAT(name: string): ANIMAL is
    super(name)

    meow() -> string =>
        "{name} says meow"
si

class DOG(name: string): ANIMAL is
    super(name)

    bark() -> string =>
        "{name} says woof"
si

class SCORE(who: string, points: int)

class ORDER(id: int, customer: CUSTOMER?)

class CUSTOMER(name: string, contact: CONTACT?)

class CONTACT(email: string)

// case over a union: when v: T gives v the variant's type for the rest
// of the arm

union SHAPE is
    CIRCLE(radius: double)
    SQUARE(side: double)
    TRIANGLE(base: double, height: double)
si

case_binding_patterns() is
    write_line("area of a circle: {area(SHAPE.CIRCLE(2.0D))}")
    write_line("area of a square: {area(SHAPE.SQUARE(3.0D))}")
    write_line("area of a triangle: {area(SHAPE.TRIANGLE(4.0D, 5.0D))}")

    write_line(is_round(SHAPE.CIRCLE(2.0D)))
    write_line(is_round(SHAPE.SQUARE(3.0D)))
si

area(s: SHAPE) -> double =>
    // SHAPE is a closed union with three variants, all covered here,
    // so this case expression is exhaustive without an else arm
    case s
    when c: SHAPE.CIRCLE then 3.14159D * c.radius * c.radius
    when q: SHAPE.SQUARE then q.side * q.side
    when t: SHAPE.TRIANGLE then 0.5D * t.base * t.height
    esac

is_round(s: SHAPE) -> string =>
    // when _: T narrows the scrutinee itself without binding a new
    // name, so s reads as SHAPE.CIRCLE inside this arm
    case s
    when _: SHAPE.CIRCLE then "round, radius {s.radius}"
    else "not round"
    esac

// a trailing '/\' guard adds a condition, checked after the pattern
// matches. when it fails, the next clause is tried, as if the pattern
// hadn't matched
if_let_guards() is
    let a_shape: SHAPE = SHAPE.CIRCLE(5.0D)

    if let c: SHAPE.CIRCLE = a_shape /\ c.radius > 1.0D then
        write_line("if let guard: big enough, radius {c.radius}")
    fi

    if let c: SHAPE.CIRCLE = a_shape /\ c.radius > 100.0D then
        write_line("unreachable")
    else
        write_line("if let guard: not big enough")
    fi
si

case_arm_guards() is
    write_line(describe_shape(SHAPE.CIRCLE(20.0D)))
    write_line(describe_shape(SHAPE.CIRCLE(2.0D)))
    write_line(describe_shape(SHAPE.SQUARE(3.0D)))
si

describe_shape(s: SHAPE) -> string =>
    // the same guard works on a case arm; the bound name (c) and the
    // scrutinee narrowing are both in scope in the guard and the body
    case s
    when c: SHAPE.CIRCLE /\ c.radius > 10.0D then "large circle"
    when c: SHAPE.CIRCLE then "circle radius {c.radius}"
    when q: SHAPE.SQUARE then "square side {q.side}"
    when t: SHAPE.TRIANGLE then "triangle base {t.base}"
    esac

// case compares its value with each label the way =~ does, so strings,
// optionals and types that declare =~ match by value, not by reference

class POINT is
    x: int
    y: int

    init(x: int, y: int) is
        self.x = x
        self.y = y
    si

    =~(other: POINT) -> bool => x == other.x /\ y == other.y
    get_hash_code() -> int => x * 397 + y
si

classify_point(p: POINT) -> string =>
    case p
    when POINT(0, 0) then "origin"
    else "elsewhere"
    esac

describe_day(name: string) -> string =>
    case name
    when "Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri" then "weekday"
    when "Sat", "Sun" then "weekend"
    else "not a day"
    esac

label_optional(n: int?) -> string =>
    // a when null label matches an absent value
    case n
    when 42 then "forty-two"
    when null then "nothing"
    else "something else"
    esac

match_by_value() is
    // built at runtime, so it's a different string object to the
    // literal "Sat" below - case still matches it by content
    let prefix = "S"
    let built = "{prefix}at"

    write_line(describe_day(built))
    write_line(describe_day("Mon"))

    // two different POINT instances, equal by =~
    write_line(classify_point(POINT(0, 0)))
    write_line(classify_point(POINT(1, 1)))

    write_line(label_optional(42))
    write_line(label_optional(null))
    write_line(label_optional(7))
si

// while let repeats the if let clause on every iteration, with the
// declared names freshly in scope each time round the loop

class LINK(value: int, next: LINK?)

sum_link(head: LINK?) -> int =>
    (
        let total mut = 0
        let current mut = head

        // a bare optional local narrows on its own presence test,
        // the same as in an if condition - no let needed here
        while current? do
            total = total + current.value
            current = current.next
        od

        total
    )

sum_until_negative(head: LINK?) -> int =>
    (
        let total mut = 0
        let current mut = head

        // while let with a name and a guard: the loop stops as soon
        // as either the chain ends or the guard fails
        while let c = current /\ c.value >= 0 do
            total = total + c.value
            current = c.next
        od

        total
    )

count_chain(head: LINK) -> int =>
    (
        let total mut = 1
        let node mut = head

        // the path shorthand declares next, matching while it holds
        while let node.next do
            total = total + 1
            node = next
        od

        total
    )

while_let_examples() is
    let chain = LINK(1, LINK(2, LINK(3, LINK(-1, LINK(4, null)))))

    write_line("sum: {sum_link(chain)}")
    write_line("sum until negative: {sum_until_negative(chain)}")
    write_line("chain length: {count_chain(chain)}")
si

// patterns nest. this is Okasaki's red-black tree rebalance, which matches a
// 4-tuple against enum values and variant patterns three levels deep

enum COLOUR is
    RED,
    BLACK,
si

union TREE is
    EMPTY
    NODE(colour: COLOUR, left: TREE, value: int, right: TREE)
si

balance(colour: COLOUR, left: TREE, value: int, right: TREE) -> TREE =>
    case (colour, left, value, right)
    when (COLOUR.BLACK, (COLOUR.RED, (COLOUR.RED, a, x, b): TREE.NODE, y, c): TREE.NODE, z, d) then
        TREE.NODE(COLOUR.RED, TREE.NODE(COLOUR.BLACK, a, x, b), y, TREE.NODE(COLOUR.BLACK, c, z, d))
    when (COLOUR.BLACK, (COLOUR.RED, a, x, (COLOUR.RED, b, y, c): TREE.NODE): TREE.NODE, z, d) then
        TREE.NODE(COLOUR.RED, TREE.NODE(COLOUR.BLACK, a, x, b), y, TREE.NODE(COLOUR.BLACK, c, z, d))
    when (COLOUR.BLACK, a, x, (COLOUR.RED, (COLOUR.RED, b, y, c): TREE.NODE, z, d): TREE.NODE) then
        TREE.NODE(COLOUR.RED, TREE.NODE(COLOUR.BLACK, a, x, b), y, TREE.NODE(COLOUR.BLACK, c, z, d))
    when (COLOUR.BLACK, a, x, (COLOUR.RED, b, y, (COLOUR.RED, c, z, d): TREE.NODE): TREE.NODE) then
        TREE.NODE(COLOUR.RED, TREE.NODE(COLOUR.BLACK, a, x, b), y, TREE.NODE(COLOUR.BLACK, c, z, d))
    else
        TREE.NODE(colour, left, value, right)
    esac

ins(t: TREE, v: int) -> TREE =>
    if let (colour, left, value, right): TREE.NODE = t then
        if v < value then
            balance(colour, ins(left, v), value, right)
        elif v > value then
            balance(colour, left, value, ins(right, v))
        else
            t
        fi
    else
        TREE.NODE(COLOUR.RED, TREE.EMPTY, v, TREE.EMPTY)
    fi

// the root of ins() may come out red; a real red-black insert always
// re-blackens the root before handing the tree back to the caller
blacken(t: TREE) -> TREE =>
    case t
    when n: TREE.NODE then TREE.NODE(COLOUR.BLACK, n.left, n.value, n.right)
    else t
    esac

insert_value(t: TREE, v: int) -> TREE => blacken(ins(t, v))

count(t: TREE) -> int =>
    case t
    when n: TREE.NODE then 1 + count(n.left) + count(n.right)
    else 0
    esac

black_height(t: TREE) -> int =>
    case t
    when n: TREE.NODE /\ n.colour == COLOUR.BLACK then 1 + black_height(n.left)
    when n: TREE.NODE then black_height(n.left)
    else 0
    esac

is_leaf(t: TREE) -> string =>
    // isa narrows t in place, and the else branch to the other variant,
    // since TREE has only two
    if isa TREE.NODE(t) then
        "node with value {t.value}"
    else
        "empty"
    fi

nested_destructuring() is
    let t: TREE mut = TREE.EMPTY
    for v in [10, 5, 20, 3, 7, 15, 25, 1, 30, 12] do
        t = insert_value(t, v)
    od

    write_line("tree size: {count(t)}")
    write_line("black height: {black_height(t)}")
    write_line(is_leaf(TREE.EMPTY))
    write_line(is_leaf(t))
si

pieces.source:
use IO.Std.write_line
use Collections

entry() is
    let int_things = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
    let string_things = ["one", "two", "three", "four", "five"]

    write_line("int_things has {count_things(int_things)} things")
    write_line("string_things has {count_things(string_things)} things")

    demonstrate_sack(SACK(), int_things)
    demonstrate_sack(SACK(), string_things)

    bounded_type_parameters()
si

bounded_type_parameters() is
    write_line(announce(CAT("Felix")))
    write_line(announce(DOG("Rex")))

    write_line(kind_of(CAT("Felix")))
    write_line(kind_of(DOG("Rex")))
si

trait Animal is
    speak() -> string
si

class CAT(name: string): Animal is
    speak() -> string => "{name} says meow"
si

class DOG(name: string): Animal is
    speak() -> string => "{name} says woof"
si

// the bound [T: Animal] means T is Animal or derives from it, so Animal's
// members can be called on a T
announce[T: Animal](pet: T) -> string =>
    pet.speak()

// isa can test a T for a particular kind of Animal directly
kind_of[T: Animal](pet: T) -> string =>
    if isa CAT(pet) then
        "a cat"
    elif isa DOG(pet) then
        "a dog"
    else
        "some other animal"
    fi

count_things[E](things: Iterable[E]) -> int is
    let count mut = 0

    for thing in things do
        count = count + 1
    od

    return count
si

trait Sack[T] is
    add(thing: T)
    count() -> int
si

class SACK[T]: Sack[T] is
    _things: MutableList[T]

    init() is
        _things = LIST()
    si

    add(thing: T) =>
        _things.add(thing)

    count() -> int =>
        _things.count
si

demonstrate_sack[T](sack: Sack[T], things: Iterable[T]) is
    for thing in things do
        sack.add(thing)
    od

    write_line("sack has {sack.count()} things")
si

pieces.source:
use IO.Std.write_line
use Collections.Iterable
use Ghul.Pipes.Pipe
use Ghul.Pipes.map
use Ghul.Pipes.filter
use Ghul.Pipes.take

// a function that returns T{} and contains yield is a generator. each yield
// produces the next value, and the function carries on from there, with its
// locals as it left them, when the next one is asked for. a generator can be
// looped over, or piped into map, filter, take and the rest.

count_up_to(n: int) -> int{} is
    let i mut = 1
    while i <= n do
        yield i
        i = i + 1
    od
si

// generators compose: this one reads another sequence and yields a running
// total:
running_totals(xs: Iterable[int]) -> int{} is
    let total mut = 0
    for x in xs do
        total = total + x
        yield total
    od
si

// the first n Fibonacci numbers. a and b keep their values across each yield:
fibonacci(n: int) -> int{} is
    let a mut = 0
    let b mut = 1
    let count mut = 0
    while count < n do
        yield a
        let c = a + b
        a = b
        b = c
        count = count + 1
    od
si

entry() is
    // loop over a generator directly
    for i in count_up_to(5) do
        write_line("count: {i}")
    od

    // or thread it through map / filter / take - all work on a generator
    write_line("squares:   {count_up_to(5) |> map(x => x * x)}")
    write_line("evens:     {count_up_to(10) |> filter(x => x % 2 == 0)}")
    write_line("first 3:   {count_up_to(100) |> take(3)}")

    // generators compose: running_totals consumes another generator
    write_line("totals:    {running_totals(count_up_to(5))}")

    // the first ten Fibonacci numbers
    write_line("fibonacci: {fibonacci(10)}")
si

count: 2
count: 3
count: 4
count: 5

topics.title: type inference
topics.intro:
ghūl infers most types, so local variables, the parameters of anonymous functions
and generic type arguments usually don't need a written type. Each program here
shows one kind of inference the compiler does.

pieces.title: local variables
pieces.source:
use IO.Std.write_line

// a let variable takes its type from its initializer:
let an_int = 42
let a_single = 3.14s
let a_double = 3.14D
let a_string = "hello"
let a_char = 'g'
let a_bool = true

write_line("an_int is a {an_int.get_type()}")
write_line("a_single is a {a_single.get_type()}")
write_line("a_double is a {a_double.get_type()}")
write_line("a_string is a {a_string.get_type()}")
write_line("a_char is a {a_char.get_type()}")
write_line("a_bool is a {a_bool.get_type()}")
pieces.output:
an_int is a System.Int32
a_single is a System.Single
a_double is a System.Double
a_string is a System.String
a_char is a System.Char
a_bool is a System.Boolean

pieces.title: for loop variables
pieces.source:
use IO.Std.write_line

// loop variables get their type from the iterable being looped over:
// i: int from the range:
for i in 1::3 do
    write_line("range value i: {i}")
od

// c: char from the string iterator:
for c in "ghul" do
    write_line("string char c: {c}")
od

// a loop variable can destructure, and each name gets its part's type:
let pairs = [("a", 1), ("b", 2), ("c", 3)]
for (name, value) in pairs do
    write_line("{name} = {value}")
od

range value i: 2
range value i: 3
string char c: g
string char c: h
string char c: u
string char c: l
a = 1
b = 2
c = 3

pieces.title: type arguments from later use
pieces.source:
use IO.Std.write_line
use Collections.LIST
use Collections.MAP

class BOX[T] is
    value: T public

    init() is si

    set(v: T) is
        value = v
    si
si

// type arguments nothing else gives can come from how the value is used later.

// T comes from the call to set:
let b = BOX()
b.set(42)
write_line("b.value: {b.value}")

// a list's element type comes from the calls to add:
let xs = LIST()
xs.add(1)
xs.add(2)
xs.add(3)
write_line("xs: {xs |> $}, count: {xs.count}")

// and a map's key and value types from assignments through its indexer:
let m = MAP()
m["one"] = 1
m["two"] = 2
m["three"] = 3
write_line("m[\"two\"]: {m["two"]}, count: {m.count}")
pieces.output:
b.value: 42
xs: [1, 2, 3], count: 3
m["two"]: 2, count: 3

pieces.title: function literal return types
pieces.source:
use IO.Std.write_line

// a function literal's return type comes from its body:
let to_message = (name: string, age: int) => "{name} is {age} years old"
write_line(to_message("ghūl", 12))

// and from its return statements where the body is a block. all three
// return a string here:
let summarise = (n: int) is
    if n == 0 then
        return "zero"
    elif n > 0 then
        return "positive"
    else
        return "negative"
    fi
si

write_line("summarise(0): {summarise(0)}")
write_line("summarise(7): {summarise(7)}")
write_line("summarise(-3): {summarise(-3)}")
pieces.output:
ghūl is 12 years old
summarise(0): zero
summarise(7): positive
summarise(-3): negative

pieces.title: union narrowing
pieces.source:
use IO.Std.write_line

union Shape is
    CIRCLE(radius: double)
    SQUARE(side: double)
si

use Shape.CIRCLE
use Shape.SQUARE

describe(s: Shape) -> string =>
    if isa CIRCLE(s) then
        // s is narrowed to CIRCLE here, so .radius is accessible:
        "circle of radius {s.radius}"
    else
        // two variants, so the else branch narrows s to SQUARE, and .side is accessible:
        "square of side {s.side}"
    fi

write_line(describe(CIRCLE(3.0D)))
write_line(describe(SQUARE(4.0D)))
pieces.output:
circle of radius 3
square of side 4
